data.title: Cookie Stuffing Detection — Affiliate Cookies Set Without Corresponding Click Events
data.description: Detects cookie stuffing — the most prevalent affiliate fraud technique (approximately 60% of cases) — by identifying affiliates that set tracking cookies in user browsers without corresponding user click events. Cookie stuffing uses hidden iframes, 1x1 pixel images, or JavaScript injection to drop affiliate cookies without the user's knowledge or intent. This steals attribution credit from legitimate affiliates and organic traffic, inflating the fraudulent affiliate's commission payments. Detection relies on the cookie-to-click ratio: legitimate affiliates typically have a ratio near 1:1, while cookie stuffers exhibit ratios of 5:1 or higher, or set cookies with zero associated clicks entirely. Global ad fraud is projected at USD 71 billion in 2025.

enrichment_required.source: Click event log correlated by session_id and affiliate_id
Computed ratio of cookies set to clicks recorded per affiliate over timeframe
DOM element that triggered the cookie (iframe, pixel, script, link)

queries.cql:
// CQL for Cookie Stuffing Detection — DL-0192
// Affiliates setting cookies without corresponding user click events
AffiliateCookies
| cookie_set_timestamp >= now() - 7d
| groupBy([affiliate_id, affiliate_name],
    function=[count() as cookies_set,
              countDistinct(session_id) as sessions,
              countDistinct(cookie_id) as unique_cookies,
              sum(if(cookie_source = "iframe" OR cookie_source = "pixel" OR cookie_source = "script", 1, 0)) as hidden_cookies,
              countDistinct(associated_click_id) as clicks_recorded])
| (clicks_recorded = 0 AND cookies_set >= 50) OR (cookies_set / max(clicks_recorded, 1)) >= 5.0
| sort(cookies_set, order=desc)
queries.sql:
-- SQL: Cookie Stuffing Detection
-- Affiliate cookies set without corresponding user click events
SELECT
  a.affiliate_id,
  a.affiliate_name,
  COUNT(DISTINCT c.cookie_id) AS cookies_set,
  COUNT(DISTINCT cl.click_id) AS clicks_recorded,
  CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT cl.click_id) = 0 THEN 999.99
       ELSE ROUND(COUNT(DISTINCT c.cookie_id) * 1.0
                  / COUNT(DISTINCT cl.click_id), 2)
  END AS cookie_to_click_ratio,
  COUNT(DISTINCT c.session_id) AS sessions_with_cookies,
  COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN c.cookie_source IN ('iframe', 'pixel', 'script')
    THEN c.cookie_id END) AS hidden_element_cookies,
  COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN sc.multi_affiliate_cookie = 1
    THEN c.session_id END) AS multi_cookie_sessions
FROM affiliate_cookies c
LEFT JOIN affiliate_clicks cl ON c.session_id = cl.session_id
  AND c.affiliate_id = cl.affiliate_id
JOIN affiliates a ON c.affiliate_id = a.affiliate_id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT session_id,
    CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT affiliate_id) > 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
      AS multi_affiliate_cookie
  FROM affiliate_cookies
  WHERE cookie_set_timestamp >= DATEADD(DAY, -7, CURRENT_DATE)
  GROUP BY session_id
) sc ON c.session_id = sc.session_id
WHERE c.cookie_set_timestamp >= DATEADD(DAY, -7, CURRENT_DATE)
GROUP BY a.affiliate_id, a.affiliate_name
HAVING (COUNT(DISTINCT cl.click_id) = 0 AND COUNT(DISTINCT c.cookie_id) >= 50)
  OR (ROUND(COUNT(DISTINCT c.cookie_id) * 1.0
      / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT cl.click_id), 0), 2) >= 5.0)
ORDER BY cookies_set DESC
queries.splunk:
`comment("Splunk SPL: Cookie Stuffing Detection")`
`comment("Affiliates setting cookies without corresponding click events")`
index=flame_advertising sourcetype=flame:affiliate_tracking
  event_type="cookie_set"
| stats count AS cookies_set,
        dc(session_id) AS sessions,
        dc(cookie_id) AS unique_cookies,
        sum(if(cookie_source="iframe" OR cookie_source="pixel"
               OR cookie_source="script", 1, 0)) AS hidden_cookies
  BY affiliate_id, affiliate_name
| join type=left affiliate_id [
    search index=flame_advertising sourcetype=flame:affiliate_tracking
      event_type="click"
    | stats dc(click_id) AS clicks_recorded BY affiliate_id
  ]
| fillnull value=0 clicks_recorded
| where (clicks_recorded=0 AND cookies_set >= 50)
  OR (cookies_set / max(clicks_recorded, 1)) >= 5.0
| sort - cookies_set

references: BluePear, Affiliate Compliance Monitoring Report (2025) — cookie stuffing prevalence
Tapper, Affiliate Fraud Trends 2025 — 60% of affiliate fraud cases
Juniper Research, Ad Fraud Market Analysis 2025 — USD 71B projection
falsepositives: Affiliates using legitimate pre-click tracking (e.g., impression-based cookies for attribution modeling)
Browser extensions that pre-load affiliate cookies with user consent
Testing and QA activity generating cookies without production click events
